name: Leave-page confirmation (beforeunload)
plain: Shows a generic Leave site? dialog, only if the person interacted with the page.
meaning: A site can ask the person to confirm closing or leaving, often to protect unsaved work. Browsers hide the site's own text, so it cannot scare people with custom messages.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt (needs a click, tap or keypress)
access.persistence: Fires on each unload attempt while the listener exists
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Dialog suppressed in cross-origin iframes without activation
steps: Person interacts with the page (sticky activation)
Page registers beforeunload and sets returnValue
On close or navigate, browser shows generic confirmation

limits.headline: Can show a generic Leave site? warning when you close or leave, after you have interacted
limits.user_action: You click, tap or type on the page, then try to close or leave it
can: Show a Leave site? box to protect your unsaved work
Show it when you close the tab or window
Show it when you press back or go to another site
cannot: Show custom text, since browsers hide the site's own message
Show the box if you have not touched the page
Block you for good, since you can still leave
limits.differs: Works in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari on computers. iPhone browsers do not show it.

story.what_it_is: A page can show a generic Are you sure you want to leave dialog, only after you used the page.

marketing.name: beforeunload event
marketing.pitch: Lets a page warn before you leave, with a standard message, only if you have interacted with it.

story.for_you: If you try to close a page with unsaved work, a box asks Leave site? You can stay or leave. Pages you never touched cannot show it.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to protect unsaved work in forms, editors and checkouts. Browsers use a fixed message to stop it being used to trap people. Misuse by scam sites is limited by the click rule.

use_cases.example: A web editor like Google Docs warns you if edits are not saved yet when you close the tab.
A checkout page asks if you want to leave with items in your cart and a half filled form.
A browser game asks before you leave a ranked match where leaving counts as a loss.
A web design tool warns about unsynced changes.
A test platform warns a student before they close an exam.
A bank page warns you before you leave a half finished transfer.
A scam page tries to trap you with repeated Leave prompts, but browsers allow it only after you click.

technical_bounds: Needs sticky user activation: no dialog if the page was never clicked or typed in (Chrome 60)
Custom message text is ignored (Chrome 51, Firefox 44, Safari 9.1)
Cannot run async work or block navigation indefinitely: dialog is the only block
A beforeunload listener makes a page ineligible for the back/forward cache in Chrome desktop and Firefox
Not reliable on mobile: tab discard and app switch skip it; use pagehide and visibilitychange

history.change: Dialog requires user interaction with the page
